Subject: Order form + SLA proposal — uptime credits & maintenance windows

Kim/Team,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're moving to finalize the order form and our legal team attached a first pass of SLA redlines focused on uptime targets, credit calculations, and maintenance notification windows. The key asks from Skyline: 99.99% for core inference (model endpoints used by product), a monthly cap on credits, and no more than two scheduled maintenance windows per quarter without an outage credit.

I've attached "Skyline_MSA_redlines_v2.docx" with inline comments — please confirm whether Redwood can accept the uptime metric and the calculation for credits in Section 4.

Quick ask: can you share Redwood's standard uptime credit matrix and whether you can guarantee 99.99 for the dedicated capacity we discussed? We're starting procurement approvals on Thursday.

Thanks,
Peter
Peter Hart
Head of Cloud Operations | Skyline Analytics

Subject: Re: Order form + SLA proposal — uptime credits & maintenance windows

Hi Peter — thanks for the note and the redlines. Looping in Karthik (sales) and Lauren (legal ops) to coordinate the response and a proposed counter on credits/maintenance. I've also copied Jordan from procurement for any order-form logistics.

Short answers up front:
- Redwood's hosted standard for inference is 99.95% for our multi-tenant offering; for Dedicated we commonly offer a contractual uptime target of 99.99% after sizing/validation.
- Our credit model is tiered and caps at 12 months of invoice value; we can share the precise matrix.
- Maintenance windows: we require at least 72 hours' notice for scheduled maintenance; additional blackout protections (e.g., product launches) can be included in the order form as exceptions.

We'll do a short internal review and come back with a redline that preserves your ask where possible and explains tradeoffs where we need to negotiate.

Can you confirm whether Skyline needs the 99.99% to apply island-wide (all endpoints) or only to a named set of endpoints (e.g., prod inference cluster)? That distinction changes the SLA controls we can put in place.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Peter Hart <peter.hart@skyline.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Sara Patel <sara.procure@skyline.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form + SLA proposal — uptime credits & maintenance windows

Peter + team,

Thanks — attached is a short uptime/credit matrix we typically propose ("uptime_credit_model_v1.xlsx"). To be explicit on negotiation points we expect:
1) Uptime target: For Dedicated deployments, we can contract 99.99% but only after a one-time onboarding validation period (30 days) and a capacity sizing statement in the order form. During the validation period we propose 99.95%.
2) Credit calculation: We prefer a %-of-monthly-invoice model with a per-incident cap and a 12-month aggregate cap. Your redline requesting a flat prorated credit with no cap is risky for us operationally.
3) Maintenance: Scheduled maintenance windows (up to 4 hours/month) will be excluded from downtime calculations if we provide >=72 hours' notice. Larger planned outages (e.g., >4 hours) will require pre-approved change windows and won't be counted as downtime provided we meet the notification terms.
4) Response times: Our standard P1 response is 15 minutes to acknowledge, 1 hour to provide initial mitigation steps, and a technical workaround SLA of 4 hours depending on root cause and customer configuration.

Next steps: Lauren, can you start with legal on a tracked counter that keeps Peter's language for the 99.99 ask but adds the validation and cap language? Jordan, once legal has a tracked counter, we'll route for procurement approval and earmark the Dedicated cluster sizing activity.

Karthik
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Attachments: uptime_credit_model_v1.xlsx

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Peter Hart <peter.hart@skyline.ai>, J. Lee <j.lee@legalpartners.com>, Sara Patel <sara.procure@skyline.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Order form + SLA proposal — SLA & maintenance counter (tracked)

Team / Peter / J. Lee — forwarding our initial tracked counter (inline comments in DocX). High-level positions I'm proposing for negotiation:
- Uptime: Agree in principle to 99.99% for Dedicated, contingent on a 30-day validation and a sizing statement. Will mark clause to specify named endpoints if that helps narrow scope (we'll add an appendix listing endpoint IDs).
- Credits: Use Redwood's tiered %-of-monthly-invoice table, per-incident cap = 200% of monthly charges for the affected service, aggregate cap = 12 months of charges. We can provide visibility into the calculation via the Console reports linked in the order form.
- Maintenance: Scheduled maintenance (<=4 hours/month) excluded when >=72 hours' notice. For emergency maintenance we will notify as soon as possible; genuine emergency maintenance (security) will be excluded from credits.
- Responses & Escalation: P1 acknowledge 15m, initial mitigation 1h, target workaround timeline to be driven by cause analysis and seasonality. We will provide a dedicated escalation path for Skyline (named contacts).

Peter — J. Lee is included in case Skyline's counsel wants to propose alternative language; please let us know which endpoints you want covered in the 99.99 target and whether your procurement team requires a separate maintenance blackout window for launch days.

I'll attach the tracked DocX in the next email.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick turn. Proposed next steps so we keep procurement on track this week:
1) Skyline to confirm whether 99.99% should apply to (a) all inference endpoints or (b) a named list of production endpoints. If you pick (b), please send the endpoint list by end of day Thursday 6/10.
2) Redwood will circulate the tracked counter (MSA + Order Form) by 6/10 COB Pacific with the uptime validation clause, credit matrix, and a maintenance appendix.
3) We propose a short call on Friday 6/11 — 30 minutes — to close open points. I'll send calendar options.

If you need the order form accelerated, Jordan is standing by to move the procurement paperwork once we have alignment on uptime scope and credit caps.

Best,
